_comment: Rail grinding (T-541, a prototype; Drifting, Content, "Rail grinding (task T-541)"). The grind's numbers, read by scripts/driving/rail_grind.gd when a car is made. All proposals for the board's playtest; the GRIND! trick's pay is in combo.json, rail_grind. Units are map units and seconds.
_catch_comment: Locking on (T-566; the board, 2026-11-07, Drifting, Decisions, "A grind starts when the car's drawing crosses the rail's"): while Space is held in the air, the car catches a rail as soon as its drawing on screen (its own opaque pixels for its heading and tilt frame, art/car/car_iso_outline.json) crosses the rail's drawn bar (3 pixel rows), whatever its height above or below the bar, rising or falling. This replaced reach (2.5), end_margin, catch_above and catch_below. Any angle catches (see _square_comment). Two rails crossed: the bar nearest the car's drawn centre on screen wins; the car lands on the point of the bar nearest that centre, so its drawing barely moves at the snap.
_square_comment: T-566, the board's answer of 2026-11-07 (Drifting, Decisions: "A crossing square-on to the rail catches too"): any crossing angle catches. A car moving along the rail at min_start_speed (2) or more grinds its own way along it at its speed along it, as before. One slower along it (square-on, or barely moving) has no speed along the rail to keep, so it grinds the way its nose points along the rail at square_start_speed, then gets the landing boost like any landing. 6 was T-548's set launch speed and is now launch_min_speed, the slowest launch (T-578): a launch that crosses the next rail square-on rides it at least as fast as the slowest launch leaves a rail (10 with the boost, just under cruise's 11), and it lasts about 4 s before end_speed, so even a short ride pays GRIND!. Since T-578 a faster launch still starts a square-on ride at 6 (the speed it brings is across the rail, not along it). A proposal for the playtest.
_slide_comment: Sliding: the speed along the rail drops by decel units/s every second; below end_speed the car drops off beside the rail at drop_side_speed. While grinding, A and D spin the car's body at the air turn rate (as in the air); it keeps sliding along the rail whichever way it faces.
_boost_comment: Landing boost (T-548; the board, 2026-11-06: "a set speed boost along the rail" on every landing, then declining). An amount added, not a speed raised to: land_boost units/s on top of the speed along the rail the car lands with, so a fast landing stays faster than a slow one and every landing feels the same push. 4 is about a third of cruise speed (11 units/s, so 15 after a cruise landing): clearly felt, still under the car's top speed of 33. The boost's part then fades at boost_decline units/s every second on top of decel (3 units/s a second in all for its first 2 s), so it is gone after land_boost / boost_decline = 2 s, about the length of a short rail at that speed; after that only decel. A joint between connected pieces is not a landing: no new boost. Proposals for the board's playtest.
_jump_comment: Launch off a rail (T-578; the board, 2026-11-08, Drifting, Decisions, "The launch off a rail keeps the grind's speed"; it replaced T-548's set 6 units/s): letting go of Space launches the car where it faces, whatever its travel along the rail (backwards too), at the speed it was grinding at that moment: the speed along the rail turns into the nose's direction. launch_min_speed is the floor, the proposal for a very slow grind: a launch never leaves slower than 6, T-548's old set speed, so a slow grind launches exactly as before. The reason: below 6 a first-tier launch (about 0.83 s in the air) carries the car under 5 units, and facing 45 degrees toward the jump pair's second rail (3.5 units away) it would no longer get across, so a slow grind would lose the rail-to-rail jump the practice playground and the tutorial teach. A grind never goes under end_speed (2) anyway, so the floor only matters between 2 and 6. Proposal for the board's playtest.
_overhaul_comment: The grind overhaul (T-551; the board, 2026-11-07, Drifting, Decisions, "The grind overhaul"). Hold Space in the air to tilt; touch a rail while holding it to grind; the grind lasts while Space stays held; letting go launches the car where it faces at the grind's speed flat (above, T-578; T-548's set 6 until then) and launch_takeoff_speed up. Any car can do it, no power-up. launch_takeoff_speed 5 is the Jump power-up's tier-1 takeoff, the hop T-548's numbers were measured with (about 0.83 s in the air, so about 5 units at the slowest launch, 6 units/s, enough to cross the jump pair's 3.5 units to the next rail); with the Jump power-up's tier 2 owned the launch uses its higher takeoff (8) instead, so the upgrade still means longer flights off a rail. Off the rail's end with Space still held the car flies on along the rail as before, stays tilted and can catch the next rail it touches (no launch: the launch is only letting go).
_tilt_comment: The tilt (T-551): 3 transition frames into the held pose, the same backwards when Space is let go in the air and on landing (the proposal: the tilt plays out on the ground as the car drives off, rather than snapping back). tilt_frame_seconds 0.06 is 3 physics steps per frame: each of the 3 frames is seen (at 2 steps the in-betweens flicker past), and the held pose is reached in 0.14 s, well inside a first-tier Jump's 0.83 s in the air.
_arrow_comment: The jump arrow (T-551; HUD and menus, Decisions, "The jump arrow"): shown while grinding (the launch is only possible on a rail), on by default (game_settings.gd). A flat arrowhead at the car's height just past its nose: its base arrow_distance units from the car's centre (the drawing is 1.5 to the nose, so 0.5 clear of it), arrow_length long and arrow_width wide (about a car's width: big enough to read, small enough not to cover the rail). Off-white with a dark outline at arrow_opacity, so it reads on the dark street and on the bar, in the Drift Guide's flat pixel look.
_effect_comment: The jump effect (T-551; Drifting, Decisions, "A jump effect around the car"): each play lasts jump_effect_seconds, about half a first-tier Jump's time in the air, so it is over before the car lands and never stacks with the next jump's.
_effect_scale_comment: The jump effect scales with the jump's height (T-590 Tweak 1; the board, 2026-11-08: 'the jump effect will be bigger depending, it scales with the jump height'). A charged hop's height over the same tier's tap height (multiplier squared: x1 at a tap, about 1.56 at half charge, 2.25 at a full charge), raised to jump_effect_height_exponent, is the effect's drawn size: 0.5 makes a full charge's effect 1.5 times as big (its area about 2.25 times, growing with the height), a half charge's 1.25. Clamped to jump_effect_max_scale. A tap and the launch off a rail draw at x1. Proposals for the playtest.
_join_comment: Joints (T-542 round 2; the board: a joint between connected rail pieces at an angle must cost no speed, and long rails curve round corners built of angled pieces). Two rails are connected when an end of one is within join_distance units (flat) of the end the car leaves by and within join_height units of its height. The car then crosses straight onto the next piece, at the same speed (nothing lost to the angle), as long as that piece's way on turns the travel by no more than join_max_angle_deg (100: a right angle and a little over, never a fold back). All proposals for the board's playtest.
